What to look at in this link
============================

Source is repro-release-crash.hlsl, not repro.hlsl. That is deliberate. Compiler Explorer
runs Release builds of DXC, so the assert this issue is titled after is compiled out there
and the description's own example exits 0 on every CE pane -- which looks like "fixed" and
is not. repro-release-crash.hlsl is the same construct with 32 locals instead of one, which
turns the same defect into a memory fault that a Release build cannot hide.

Three panes, chosen to straddle the introduction:

  dxc 1.7.2212   exit 0        -- last release before the analysis existed
  dxc 1.7.2308   SIGSEGV       -- first release containing 1380cf88e
  dxc trunk      SIGSEGV       -- still present

Scope and limits of this link:

  * CE corroborates; it does not overrule the local build. The verdict in this triage rests
    on the local Debug build of 13730886e, which asserts (0xE0000001). CE cannot show that
    assert at all, because it has no Debug DXC.
  * CE's crash is SIGSEGV on Linux; locally the same source gives 0xC0000005 on the shipped
    Windows v1.9.2607 binary. Same class of fault -- an out-of-bounds access -- reached by
    two independent toolchains, which is why it is worth citing.
  * The 1.7.2212 pane is a genuine negative, not a missing feature: it compiles the file and
    exits 0. HLSL 2021 templates are available from 1.6.2112 onward, so every pane here can
    actually parse the source. Releases at or below 1.6.2106 cannot, and are excluded.
